prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Weekly On-Call Rotation Schedule (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Week 14(Mar 30 – Apr 5)" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Week 15(Apr 6 – 12)" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Week 16(Apr 13 – 19)" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Week" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 119px
  col 2: header "Role" · longest unbreakable word 78px · one-line width 78px
  col 3: header "Engineer" · longest unbreakable word 91px · one-line width 129px
  col 4: header "Phone" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 132px
  col 5: header "Escalation notes" · longest unbreakable word 89px · one-line width 655px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Show who is on call each week, how to reach them, and what to do when an issue needs escalation.","reading":"Readers find the current week, distinguish primary from secondary coverage, then follow the row to the engineer, phone number and escalation instructions. The week cells span both roles, so their height can absorb some wrapping.","groups":["Week and Role establish the coverage period and priority; each week groups a primary and secondary row.","Engineer and Phone identify and contact the person assigned to each role.","Escalation notes give the follow-up instructions associated with each assignment."],"keep_intact":["Phone numbers should remain recognizable and preferably on one line for reliable dialing.","Engineer names and role labels should remain whole where possible.","Week numbers and date ranges should remain easy to associate with their two rows."],"may_wrap":["Escalation notes can wrap at word boundaries.","Week labels and date ranges can occupy separate lines within the merged cells.","Engineer names can wrap between words if needed."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [90, 99, 112, 153, 220] · table 675×580px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 106, 83, 83, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 315px
Design r1B: widths [80, 99, 112, 153, 180] · table 625×720px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 129, 106, 106, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 265px
Design r1C: widths [90, 99, 150, 153, 200] · table 693×673px · row heights [36, 106, 106, 129, 83, 106, 106] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 333px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
